requirement:
`languages::Rust` implements `OutlineLang` under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider`. Its default value is
cheaply cloneable and claims `.rs`. Filename-based constructors select it under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.defaults`.
rationale:
The `requirements.sdk.sources.rust.language` text has four obligations. The marked test `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline]` covers each of them for `languages::Rust`. It does this through the generic `check` helper, which is called with `languages::Rust`, `"a.RS"`, `"fn check() {}"`, the selector `"fn[check]"`, extensions `["rs"]` and scheme `"rust-structural-v1"`.

- **Implements `OutlineLang`.** `check` is bounded by `L: OutlineLang + Default + Copy`, so the call only compiles if `Rust` implements the trait and is `Default` and `Copy`. The test also calls `name`, `extensions`, `fingerprint_scheme`, `outline` and `search_structure` and asserts on their results. The raw outline's first item spans the whole source, and its selectors and diagnostic match the explicit `OutlineContent::from_source_with` result.
- **Default value cheaply cloneable.** The test uses `Default` (`L::default().fingerprint_scheme()`) and asserts `size_of::<L>() == 0`, so cloning owns no allocation. It also clones the value and checks the clone's extensions.
- **Claims `.rs`.** `assert_eq!(language.extensions(), expected_extensions)` pins the list to exactly `["rs"]`, with no leading dot.
- **Filename-based constructors select it.** `OutlineContent::from_source` is called with `a.RS` and with `not-present.RS`, which is the claimed extension upper-cased. The test checks that the result's fingerprint equals the explicit Rust result's fingerprint. It also checks that the scheme is Rust's, that the root selector is empty and spans the source, and that `select("fn[check]")` succeeds. A plain-text fallback would fail these checks, because plain text yields no `fn[check]` item. Matching on the upper-cased extension also checks that matching is case-insensitive, as `requirements.sdk.outlines.defaults` requires.

`OutlineContent::from_path` is also a filename-based constructor, and the test doesn't call it. I read it in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/contents.rs#impl[OutlineContent]/fn[from_path]`. It has no inference logic of its own and calls `Self::parse_source(path, source)`. That makes a separate test of it unnecessary.

I found no requirement-violating behavior that this test would accept, so I report no gap.

text: cheaply cloneable and claims `.rs`. Filename-based constructors select it under
`OutlineLang` defines the language interface. Each implementation supplies its
name, claimed extensions, and outlining operation. Cloning a language shares
its prepared configuration instead of rebuilding it or copying it in proportion
to its size. Its result uses the public items, spans, and hashes under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.items`. Filename extensions omit the leading dot.
The filename-based constructors include Rust, Python, TypeScript, TSX,
Markdown, CSS, TOML, and YAML languages. Extension matching is
case-insensitive, using each implementation's claimed extensions.
A filename without a claimed extension uses the
